WRS Raipur · Spring & Wagon QC · the DRM, on the laptop

DRM walk — every screen, step by step

Before you start — five minutes, once

  1. On the shop PC, double‑click START.cmd; it prints the address for the tablet.
  2. On the tablet, turn mobile data off and join the shop Wi‑Fi.
  3. Install the certificate on the tablet once — server\certs\lan‑cert.crt, as in TABLET_TRUST.md — so the address opens with no warning and the camera and offline mode are allowed.
  4. Open the address START.cmd printed and accept Add to home screen.
  5. Sign in with the DRM account.

Then go step by step. Each step shows the screen as it should look, the taps in order, what must be on your screen, and what to suspect when it is not. Tick Seen it only when you saw it.

The dashboards

4.1 – 4.4

Sign in as the DRM. Every figure from the record, with its count.

4.1

Shop Floor — Right Now

Seen it

Do

  1. Sign in with the account you were given.
  2. Tap DRM Dashboard. Read the tiles under Shop Floor — Right Now.

You must see

  • When does today's pile finish? — springs per hour and the hours for the shift's pile, with how many sorted over how many minutes.
  • How many bogies can we build right now? — the number, and which spring position is the limit.
  • What will Stores need this fortnight? — replacements across so many wagons, with the observed condemnation rate and the number of inspections it rests on.
  • Is the record intact? — yes, N entries, unbroken.
  • None says Not yet known.

What it proves

Four questions a DRM actually asks, answered from the record with the basis under each. Where the evidence would be thin the tile says "not yet known" instead of a number — on the demo record it is not thin.

Checked on the build verified · 05:07:08 pm

  • the "Shop Floor — Right Now" section
  • when today's pile finishes, with the rate
  • how many bogies can be built
  • what Stores will need
  • none says "Not yet known"

If it is not there

  • A tile says "Not yet known": the bench has too few springs today — sort a few as the inspector first, or re-seed.
4.2

The rest of the dashboard

Seen it

Do

  1. Scroll.

You must see

  • What a camera could tell an inspector — blind-read agreement, assembly coverage, the pocket-count dataset: what has been earned and what has not.
  • Where wagons wait — dwell per stage with the median and the slow stage; the wagon that will miss its date, computed from the stages left, not predicted.
  • What keeps coming back — recurring findings by part and wagon type.
  • Turnaround, the band distribution (six colours, the bench included), inspector quality, gauge exposure — every rate with its count.

What it proves

Every figure carries its n. Nothing here is a forecast or a model's number.

Checked on the build verified · 05:07:15 pm

  • turnaround
  • where wagons wait — and the wagon that will miss its date
  • what keeps coming back
  • inspector quality
  • gauge exposure
  • rates carry their counts
4.3

Spring Analytics

Seen it

Do

  1. Spring Analytics. Tap one of the day bars.
  2. Scroll to the standard report and the gauge drift panel.

You must see

  • Bench totals today and this week; tapping a bar reads that day's figures beneath it.
  • Stock by band.
  • The standard report — this shop's springs against the G‑95 bands, with n on every figure.
  • Gauge drift names OSG‑02: the two outer gauges disagree by 1.5 mm — put both against the master.

What it proves

The distribution of a shop's springs against the standard is evidence RDSO has never had from a shop; the drift check finds a gauge reading high from the record alone.

4.4

What the system has learned

Seen it

Do

  1. System Learning. Read the table. Tap Run Analysis.

You must see

  • Each subsystem — caliper reading, spring classification, voice, acoustic, defect suggestions, the amber box, wagon-number reading, spring camera, part camera — with observations, corrections and accuracy. On the demo record: no data.
  • The camera has not been taught anything yet. The server confirms the camera may not sort on its own.
  • After Run Analysis, a green line: Analysed at HH:MM — N observations, 0 new proposals (nothing worth changing yet).
  • RDSO band tables and condemning limits are never tunable — they are regulation, not parameters.

What it proves

What has been learned is a table with counts, not a claim. No change applies itself; each is accepted by a named supervisor. The standard is never "learned".

Checked on the build verified · 05:07:24 pm

  • each subsystem with its observations, corrections and accuracy
  • the camera says it has not been taught anything yet
  • the server confirms the camera may not sort on its own (allowed: ?)
  • after Run Analysis: "Analysed at 5:07:29 pm — 0 observations, 0 new proposals (nothing worth changing yet)."

If it is not there

  • Run Analysis shows an error: the server refused the DRM — report it; it was fixed on 21 Sep.

Oversight — what the DRM can see and cannot do

Seen it

What it proves

Oversight sees everything and writes nothing.

4.8

What the DRM cannot do

Seen it

Do

  1. Wagons Pipeline. Look for a Register button.

You must see

  • There is no Register New Wagon button — and the server refuses the DRM's sign-in for it too (403).
  • As a supervisor: a junk number is refused; a wagon registered by mistake is voided with Registered in error? — reason, one-time code — and leaves the pipeline while its record stays.

What it proves

The record is always written by the floor. Oversight cannot register or inspect, so a figure on the DRM's dashboard is never the DRM's own entry.

Checked on the build verified · 05:07:53 pm

  • no Register New Wagon button
  • the server refuses the DRM's token: 403

If it is not there

  • A Register button on the DRM's pipeline: a permission fault — report it.
4.9

A certificate that proves itself

Seen it

Do

  1. Open SECR/BOXNHL/10492 → Release Certificate.
  2. Scan the QR with the phone on the same Wi‑Fi.

You must see

  • The phone opens the verify page and shows VERIFIED — the signature checked against the shop's key in the phone's own browser.
  • The same page also takes a certificate file with no server at all — what another railway would do.

What it proves

No login, no server, no trust in this laptop: the certificate carries its proof.

Checked on the build verified · 05:07:57 pm

  • the QR is a link to the verify page
  • the verify page shows VERIFIED: "Verify a release certificate or a wagon passport Checked here, in this browser, with no request to a…"

By hand: The verify page was opened and checked from the laptop; scanning it needs the phone.

If it is not there

  • The phone opens the app's sign-in screen instead: the phone holds an old copy of the app — open the address once more and it updates.
